questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in going to Berlin to experience studying theatre and performance in a place where this field of studying is broader and have a variety of possibilities to engage in, being a leading cultural metropolitan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had a hard time finding the information I needed and it is very dependent on your own effort to figure out what to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The were some Orientation days and some emails coming out about the first week there, but then once you had to choose the courses the information was very limited.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was told that it would be very hard, but I found a bunch of Facebook groups for danish people, where I managed to find an apartment for my whole stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend living in the city and experiencing that site of Berlin. And find WG where you still have some people around you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything up to the point of arriving on the school and choosing courses was easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was Orientation days and an online orientation zoom call with all exchange students, but it was very general information and hard to adapt to your individual study plan.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was honestly very hard to figure out the course registration and I spend a lot of time on it. I ended up having to change my courses several times so to the lack of information about ects credits.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would definitely hook up with other exchange students and help each other out and especially students who have the same requirements as you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think there was a huge different on the levels on the different courses, especially the exchange courses were less demanding than the seminars from my field of studying.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Since the structure is very different because you have 6-8 courses instead of 2 in one semester, so the individual courses are less demanding, but you have more information in generel to have an overview over. The teaching was more strict and attendance was mandatory, where I am used to way more flexibility and individual study time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Berlin city of water
- Creative Writing
- Places and non Places
- Formwandel des Theaters im 20. JH
- Neue Forschungsansätze zur Tanzmoderne
- Space and spatial studies 
- Hybride Beziehungen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The practical seminars are very Nice and social for Exchange students to engange in. And also the Places and non Places and the Creative writing class was very good and Creative approaches.

questions.answer: I brought my bike and had to fix that and spend 90 euros on dentist appointments

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is in general cheaper, which is great.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were fu-sports Club and some social events and gatherings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend doing some sport acticity in the city like bouldering or dancing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to sorrounding nature parks in Germany and do small hikes and trips out from the city. There are a lot of events happening around Berlin as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since it was a very international community it was easy within that, but harder with the local German culture if you don’t speak the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do activities and be open!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People where not as open as polite as I was used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: In general are people who live in Berlin more openminded to diversity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be social and engage in activities. Ask people for help! Plan trips on the weekend with people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan ahead and check out the courses in good time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from other cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being overstimulated socially and having to take breaks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
